## SERVICES & SUBSCRIPTIONS TIMELINE (Quick Reference)
* **4 Weeks Out (J):** Cancel local Ohio memberships (gyms, local clubs, car wash passes) that have a 30-day notice policy.
* **2 Weeks Out (P):** Submit USPS Change of Address. Notify auto/renters insurance, banks, credit cards, and HR/payroll of your upcoming address change.
* **2 Weeks Out (M):** Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs (Electric, Gas, Water, Trash, Internet) for the day *after* your move-out date. Schedule Oregon utility turn-ons for the day *before* you arrive.
* **1 Week Out (P):** Update shipping addresses on Amazon, Chewy (for the dog!), and any subscription boxes. Transfer prescriptions to an Oregon pharmacy chain.
* **Post-Move (J):** Return Ohio internet/cable equipment (get a receipt!). Update driver's licenses, voter registration, and loyalty accounts.

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING & DECLUTTERING CHECKLIST

### Cross-Country Decluttering Rules of Thumb
Moving weight/volume across 2,400 miles is expensive. Before putting an item in a box, ask:
1. **The Cost-to-Move Test:** Movers charge roughly $0.50–$1.00 per pound for cross-country moves. Does that $40 particle-board bookshelf weigh 60 lbs? Sell it or donate it, and buy another in Oregon.
2. **The Climate Check:** Depending on where in Oregon you are moving (e.g., the Willamette Valley/Portland vs. High Desert/Bend), you may trade heavy Ohio snow gear for high-quality rain shells and layers. Ditch worn-out winter gear.
3. **The Prohibited Items Rule:** Movers *cannot* legally transport flammables, aerosols, propane tanks, bleach, paint, or ammunition. Use them up or give them to neighbors now.

### Room-by-Room Breakdown

**1. Garage, Basement, & Storage (Pack in Weeks 6–5)**
*Priority: HIGH (Takes the longest to sort) | Est. Time: 6–10 hrs | Resp: **J***
- [ ] **Declutter:** Dispose of paints, motor oils, weed killers, and propane tanks. Sell/donate duplicate tools and unused sports gear.
- [ ] **M:** Drain fuel and oil from any gas-powered lawn equipment (if taking it). Clean garden tools.
- [ ] **P:** Pack holiday decorations, camping gear, and seasonal items. 
- [ ] **J:** Bundle long-handled tools together with zip-ties or shrink wrap. Pack heavy hand tools in *small* boxes so the bottoms don't blow out.

**2. Guest Room, Office, & Living Room Decor (Pack in Weeks 5–4)**
*Priority: MED | Est. Time: 4–6 hrs | Resp: **P***
- [ ] **Declutter:** Recycle old paperwork, shred outdated tax docs (older than 7 years), and donate books you won't read again (books are heavy!).
- [ ] **P:** Pack books flat in small boxes (prevents spine damage and back injuries).
- [ ] **P:** Wrap framed art and mirrors in bubble wrap and use picture boxes. Mark glass with a big "X" in masking tape to prevent shattering.
- [ ] **M:** Photograph the back of your TV/computer setups so you remember how cords plug in. Pack electronics in original boxes if you have them, or wrap heavily in anti-static bubble wrap/blankets. Remove batteries from all remotes/devices.

**3. Bedrooms & Closets (Pack in Weeks 3–2)**
*Priority: MED | Est. Time: 4–6 hrs | Resp: **J** (Each packs their own)*
- [ ] **Declutter:** If it doesn't fit, is stained, or hasn't been worn in 12 months, donate it.
- [ ] **J:** Set aside 10–14 days of clothes (plus layers for changing weather along the drive) to go in suitcases.
- [ ] **J:** Use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes to save hours of ironing later, or leave them on hangers and pull heavy-duty trash bags up around them in bundles of 10.
- [ ] **P:** Pack shoes in original boxes or stuff them with socks and put them in medium boxes.
- [ ] **M:** Place all jewelry, watches, and heirlooms in a container to go *in your car*, never on the moving truck.

**4. Kitchen & Dining Room (Pack in Weeks 2–1)**
*Priority: HIGH (Most fragile and time-consuming) | Est. Time: 8–12 hrs | Resp: **J***
- [ ] **Declutter:** Toss expired pantry items, mismatched Tupperware, chipped mugs, and duplicate utensils. Plan meals for the last 2 weeks to eat down the freezer and pantry.
- [ ] **J:** Pack dishes and glasses vertically (like records) in dish-pack boxes with plenty of packing paper between each item. They are much less likely to break on their edges than stacked flat.
- [ ] **M:** Pack small appliances (toaster, blender, mixer), taping cords to the sides.
- [ ] **P:** Set aside a "Paper Plate Kit" for the last 4 days (paper plates, plastic forks, 1 pan, 1 spatula, coffee maker) and pack the rest of the kitchen completely.

**5. Bathrooms & Laundry (Pack in Week 1)**
*Priority: LOW (Quick to pack) | Est. Time: 2–3 hrs | Resp: **M***
- [ ] **Declutter:** Toss expired medications, old makeup, and nearly-empty shampoo bottles.
- [ ] **M:** Place plastic wrap under the caps of any liquids you are keeping, then screw the caps back on and put them in Ziploc bags (altitude changes in the Rockies/Cascades will make bottles leak!).
- [ ] **M:** Pack extra towels and linens in large boxes (use them as padding for fragile items if needed). Keep 1 towel per person (and 2 for the dog) out for the final days.

**6. The "Open First" Box (Pack 2 Days Out)**
*Priority: HIGH | Est. Time: 1 hr | Resp: **J***
- [ ] Pack one clear plastic bin (so you can see it immediately) to go in the trunk of your car or loaded dead-last on the truck: Toilet paper, paper towels, all-purpose cleaner, trash bags, box cutters, phone chargers, basic tool kit (Allen wrenches/screwdrivers for furniture), bedsheets for night one, coffee maker + mugs + coffee, and bath towels.

---

## 8-WEEK CALENDAR OF REMINDERS (Phone-Sync Ready)
*Copy and paste these into your phone's calendar or reminders app. Set alerts for 9:00 AM on the designated Saturdays and Tuesdays so you can tackle admin tasks on weekdays and heavy lifting on weekends.*

* **8 Weeks Out (Saturday):** `[J] Finalize and book Mover/Truck + Car Shipping. Pay deposits.`
* **8 Weeks Out (Tuesday):** `[M] Schedule Oregon internet install & research utility providers.`
* **7 Weeks Out (Saturday):** `[J] Book dog-friendly hotels along driving route (aim for ~400–500 miles/day).`
* **7 Weeks Out (Tuesday):** `[M] Vet appointment: Get dog's vaccines, rabies cert, and microchip info printed.`
* **6 Weeks Out (Saturday):** `[J] Declutter & pack Garage/Storage (6–10 hrs). Order boxes & tape.`

* **4 Weeks Out (Saturday):** `[J] Donate/dispose of garage hazmat items & thrift store pile.`
* **4 Weeks Out (Tuesday):** `[J] Cancel local Ohio gyms/memberships. Notify employers of exact move dates.`

* **3 Weeks Out (Tuesday):** `[M] Call auto/renters insurance to set up Oregon policies for move-in date.`

* **1 Day Out (Friday):** `[M] Pick up rental truck (if DIY) OR clear pathways for movers. Load car essentials.`

---

# PRINTABLE ONE-PAGE: MOVING DAY & ROAD TRIP ESSENTIALS
*(Print this page, tape it to the kitchen counter during pack-up, and keep it in the glovebox for the drive to Oregon.)*

### 1. DO NOT PUT ON THE TRUCK (Load in Car First!)
- [ ] **The Master Document Folder:** Leases/closing docs, IDs/passports, Birth/Marriage certs, SS cards, Car titles, Moving Bill of Lading, Vet records.
- [ ] **Valuables & Electronics:** Laptops, tablets, jewelry, small heirlooms, external hard drives, spare car keys.
- [ ] **Medications:** 2-week supply of all human and dog prescriptions + basic first-aid kit (Ibuprofen, band-aids, antacids).
- [ ] **Suitcases:** 10–14 days of weather-appropriate clothes, toiletries, comfortable shoes, rain jackets.
- [ ] **The "Open First" Clear Bin:** Sheets, towels, toilet paper, box cutter, basic tools, trash bags, charger cords.

### 2. DOG CO-PILOT KIT (Keep in Backseat/Accessible)
- [ ] Crash-tested harness/seatbelt tether or secured crate + backseat hammock.
- [ ] Collar with current ID tags + a backup leash (keep one leash looped on the front seat headrest for quick pit stops).
- [ ] 1-week supply of regular dog food + high-value treats + 1 gallon of Ohio tap water (sudden water changes can cause an upset stomach on the road) + collapsible bowls.
- [ ] Poop bags, paper towels, pet-safe enzyme cleaner, and an old towel for muddy paws.
- [ ] Favorite blanket/bed (unwashed, so it smells like home for hotel rooms) + chew toys + calming aids/meds from vet.

### 3. VEHICLE & ROAD EMERGENCY KIT
- [ ] Spare tire (checked for air), jack, jumper cables/portable jump-starter, tire pressure gauge.
- [ ] Flashlight/headlamp, windshield fluid, ice scraper (mountain passes in WY/ID/OR can have freak weather even in shoulder seasons).
- [ ] Cooler with bottled water, high-protein road snacks, and cash/quarters for tolls or emergencies.
- [ ] Paper map/downloaded offline Google Maps for Wyoming, Idaho, and Eastern Oregon dead zones.

### 4. FINAL OHIO HOUSE WALK-THROUGH (Before Locking Up)
- [ ] **Movers:** Walk every room with the crew lead. Check all closets, attic, basement, garage, dishwasher, and under sinks.
- [ ] **Sign Paperwork:** Verify the destination address and your phone number on the Bill of Lading. Get your signed copy.
- [ ] **Clean & Document:** Sweep/vacuum empty rooms. Take timestamped photos/video of every clean, empty room and the inside of the fridge/oven (protects your security deposit).
- [ ] **Utilities & Climate:** Set thermostat to landlord’s requested temp (or 55°F in winter / 80°F in summer). Turn off water shutoff valve if leaving the property vacant.
- [ ] **Secure the Property:** Check all windows and back doors are locked. Turn off all lights and ceiling fans.
- [ ] **Meter Reads:** Take a photo of final electric, gas, and water meter readings.
- [ ] **Keys:** Leave keys, garage openers, and parking passes in the designated spot (take a photo of them sitting there) or hand them to the landlord.

### 5. CRITICAL CONTACTS (Fill in before leaving)

## 1. PACKING SUPPLIES MASTER LIST (1–2 Bedroom + Garage)

### Tape, Wrap, & Hardware (Joint Shopping List — **M** to pick up)
* **Packing Tape:** 6–8 rolls of heavy-duty acrylic or hot-melt packing tape + **2 tape guns** (one for **M**, one for **P**—do not share a tape gun, it causes arguments!). *Skip cheap dollar-store tape; it peels off in hot/cold trucks.*
* **Packing Paper:** Two 10-lb boxes of unprinted newsprint (about 400 sheets total). *Do not use real newspaper on dishes; the ink rubs off and means you have to wash everything in Oregon.*
* **Bubble Wrap:** 1–2 large rolls (100–150 ft total of 3/16" small bubble) for frames, electronics, and heirlooms.
* **Stretch Wrap:** 2 rolls of 5-inch or 15-inch plastic stretch wrap (with handles). Use this to wrap furniture drawers shut, bundle curtain rods, and protect upholstered furniture from dirt.
* **Furniture Pads:** 12–24 moving blankets (if doing DIY truck/PODS; full-service movers provide their own).
* **Labeling:** 4 thick black Sharpies + 1 multipack of colored Painter’s Tape or Colored Duct Tape (see labeling system below).

### Estimated Supply Costs
* **All-New Retail Route:** **$220 – $350** (Buying every box, roll of tape, and specialty carton brand-new).
* **The Smart Hybrid Route (Recommended):** **$90 – $150** (Getting 50–70% of standard boxes for free/reused, buying tape, paper, and specialty TV/dish boxes new).

---

## 2. WHERE TO BUY: BIG BOX vs. THRIFT/USED vs. FREE

### What to Buy at Big Box Hardware (Home Depot, Lowe’s, Menards) & U-Haul
* **Best for:** New standard boxes, Dish Barrel boxes, TV/Mirror boxes, and packing paper.
* **Why:** Home Depot and Lowe’s are consistently the cheapest for new boxes ($1.25–$2.75 per standard box) and offer "Heavy Duty" double-walled options worth getting for kitchen items.
* **Pro Tip (U-Haul Buy-Back Policy):** U-Haul stores have the best selection of specialty boxes (wardrobe, dish-saver kits) and **they offer a 100% buy-back guarantee on any unused boxes and unopened supplies** as long as you keep the receipt. Overbuy by 15% at U-Haul, and return what you don't use the day before you leave.

### Where to Buy Bulk / Discount (Amazon, Walmart, Harbor Freight)
* **Tape & Bubble Wrap:** Buy multipacks of Scotch Heavy Duty tape and 150-ft rolls of bubble wrap on Amazon or at Walmart/Costco—they are 30–40% cheaper than at hardware stores.
* **Moving Blankets & Stretch Wrap (If DIY):** **Harbor Freight** is the gold mine for DIY movers. Their 72" x 80" padded moving blankets go on sale for $6–$9 each (cheaper than renting them for a one-way trip!), and their giant rolls of stretch wrap and ratcheting tie-down straps are rock-bottom priced.

### Where to Get FREE (or Dirt-Cheap) Boxes
* **Facebook Marketplace, Nextdoor, & "Buy Nothing" Groups (Best Source!):** People who just moved into your Ohio neighborhood are desperate to get rid of stacks of once-used U-Haul/Home Depot boxes and packing paper. Check daily starting 6 weeks out (**P** can monitor these).
* **Liquor Stores:** Ask the manager early in the week for wine and liquor boxes. They are small, extraordinarily sturdy (built to hold heavy glass), and often come with cardboard cell dividers inside—perfect for glasses, mugs, pantry jars, and books.
* **Grocery Stores (Produce & Egg Boxes):** Ask the produce department for **apple and banana boxes** (bring heavy-duty paper to cover the ventilation holes on the bottom) or **egg crates**. They have built-in handles and are crush-proof for heavy garage items.
* **Bookstores (Barnes & Noble / Local Shops):** Their shipment boxes are small, uniform, and reinforced to hold heavy weight.
* **What to AVOID for a Cross-Country Move:** Do not use flimsy cereal/diaper boxes, random Amazon boxes of 30 different sizes (impossible to stack tightly in a truck), or grocery boxes that ever held raw meat or leaky produce (attracts pests in transit).

---

## 3. THE "NO-BRAINER" COLOR-CODED LABELING SYSTEM

When you arrive in Oregon tired, you don't want movers (or each other) asking *"Where does this go?"* 80 times. Use a **Color + Number** system.

### Step 1: Assign Colored Tape to Every Room
Buy a multipack of 6 colors of duct tape or wide painter's tape. Stick a piece of colored tape on **two adjacent sides** of every box (never just the top—you can't see the top when boxes are stacked 6 feet high!). At the Oregon house, stick a strip of the matching color on the doorframe of each room before unloading begins.

* 🔴 **RED Tape** = Kitchen & Dining *(Packed/Labeled by: **J**)*
* 🔵 **BLUE Tape** = Primary Bedroom & Bath *(Packed/Labeled by: **J**)*
* 🟢 **GREEN Tape** = Living Room & Office *(Packed/Labeled by: **P**)*
* 🟡 **YELLOW Tape** = Guest Room / Hall Closets *(Packed/Labeled by: **P**)*
* 🟠 **ORANGE Tape** = Garage, Patio, & Tools *(Packed/Labeled by: **M**)*
* 🟣 **PURPLE Tape (or Stars!)** = **OPEN FIRST / DOG ESSENTIALS** *(Packed/Labeled by: **J**)*

### Step 2: Number the Boxes & Keep a Phone Master List
Instead of writing every single item on the outside of the box (which takes forever and advertises valuables like *"PS5 and Jewelry"* to strangers), write a **Room Code + Box Number** on the tape (e.g., **K-01, K-02** for Kitchen; **LR-01** for Living Room) and type the detailed contents into a shared Google Sheet or Apple Note on your phones. If you desperately need the dog’s nail clippers or the router power cord in week one, just hit `Ctrl+F` on your phone to see exactly which numbered box it's in.
